clue.text: Check on tax for strong drink

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' means placed after the other piece

parts.note: scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone checks the duty charged on a bottle of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky distilled in Scotland is the classic strong spirit.

clue.text: Flower for Harlequin's sweetheart

explanation.surface: A posy bought for a pantomime clown's girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a garden plant of the buttercup family and the pantomime heroine loved by Harlequin.

clue.text: Note deformation on new piece of wood

indicators.note: a deformation bends the shape of the word note into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A carpenter spots a warp on a freshly cut timber joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deformation' looks like damage to the wood, but it signals an anagram of 'Note'; 'on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In joinery the projecting tongue cut to fit a mortise is a shaped piece of timber.

clue.text: With horse, ride fast, coming a cropper… thus?

definitions.text: With horse, ride fast, coming a cropper… thus?

parts.note: H is slang shorthand for heroin, called horse

indicators.note: to come a cropper is to fall badly, so the letters tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider galloping too hard takes a fall and lands awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming a cropper' scrambles RIDE FAST behind H; the whole clue then describes how a thrown rider lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thrown off a galloping mount typically hits the ground leading with the skull, which is the manner described.

clue.text: Historical movement — it's represented in unruly march

indicators.note: in tells us one group of letters goes inside the other
an unruly march is a disorderly one, so its letters are jumbled
represented here means set out again in another form, a second rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a rowdy protest march stands for a political cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns MARCH into CHARM, and 'represented' turns IT'S into TIS, which goes 'in' to give CHAR-TIS-M.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineteenth-century British working-class campaign for the People's Charter is a famous reform movement.

clue.text: Nourishment suitable for ladies or gents?

definitions.text: Nourishment suitable for ladies or gents?

parts.words: Nourishment suitable for ladies or gents?
parts.note: ladies and gents are public toilets, which the British call conveniences, so food suitable for them is a quick ready meal

explanation.surface: A menu offers dishes fit for men and women alike.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public lavatory is a 'convenience', and signs read 'Ladies' and 'Gents'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made meals that need little preparation are sold as nourishment offering ease.

clue.text: Prize in a raffle that is set up

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means the word is written upwards, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: a raffle is a draw for prizes

explanation.surface: A ticket-holder wins something in a raffle that has been rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' signals reversal only in a down clue, where the word reads upwards; 'that is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy or honour given to a winner is a prize.

clue.text: Sign chap's absorbed in wordy book

indicators.note: absorbed in means taken inside the other word

parts.note: Taurus is a sign of the zodiac
chap's is he's, a chap being he

explanation.surface: A man is engrossed in a horoscope found in a long-winded tome.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference work of synonyms is literally a book full of words.

clue.text: Closely follow speaker's initial address

indicators.note: initial picks out the first letter of the word speaker's

parts.note: to give an address is to give a talk

explanation.surface: Someone tracks the opening words of a speech carefully.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow someone persistently and secretly is to pursue them closely.

clue.text: Having plot, can put in a variety of banana

parts.note: a plot is a scheme or plan

indicators.note: put in means the letter goes inside the word for can

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A gardener with an allotment wants to grow some exotic fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy cooking banana is one kind of the fruit.

clue.text: Guitarist fluffed an exam

indicators.note: to fluff something is to bungle it, so the letters come out muddled

explanation.surface: A rock musician failed a test he sat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock slang calls a guitar an axe, so a player is named after it.

clue.text: Island's recreation areas joined together? That's novel

parts.note: the Isle of Man, so Man's
a field is an area for games
a park is an area for leisure

explanation.surface: A holiday isle's playgrounds are linked up, which is a new idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the definition, a Jane Austen book.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1814 book about Fanny Price is a work of fiction.

clue.text: Sherry stashed away by staff in office

indicators.note: stashed away by says the letters lie concealed inside the following words

explanation.surface: A bottle of fortified wine is hidden by employees at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale dry Spanish fortified wine is a type of sherry.

clue.text: Wealthy set loves cars for scrambling

indicators.note: scrambling mixes up the letters of the words given

explanation.surface: Rich people adore motor cars for off-road racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The richest social group, sitting above all others, is a privileged elite.

clue.text: Dope obtained in most unusual part of Brazil, perhaps

indicators.note: obtained in means put inside the other word

parts.note: rarest means most unusual
dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: Drugs found in an odd corner of a South American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs; here it means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon jungle covers much of Brazil, an example of dense tropical woodland.

clue.text: Uncomplicated charge, initially, for land tenure

indicators.note: initially says the charge comes first, at the start

parts.note: a charge is a fee
uncomplicated means simple

explanation.surface: A straightforward fee is paid up front for holding property.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, outright ownership of an estate with no conditions is the fullest form of landholding.

clue.text: Position newspaper employee's taken over drug

indicators.note: in a down clue taken over places this piece above the other

parts.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper
a stance is a position

explanation.surface: A journalist takes a stand on narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug, especially an illegal one, is often called a controlled chemical.

clue.text: Runs out of door at rear of theatre, showing remorse

indicators.note: at rear of says the door piece comes after the theatre

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: out of means taken away from the word for door

parts.note: a door is an entrance
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone flees through a back door of the playhouse, full of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow for wrongdoing is contrition.

clue.text: Boarding ship, old boy sounds upset

indicators.note: boarding means going inside, here inside the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A former pupil getting onto a vessel seems distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Weeping noisily is making distressed noises.

clue.text: Bigwig living outside Cologne's boundaries, a potential political leader?

indicators.note: outside means the bigwig goes round the letters

parts.note: VIP is a very important person

indicators.note: boundaries means the first and last letters of Cologne

parts.note: living somewhere makes you a resident

explanation.surface: A big shot who lives outside a German city might one day run the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The deputy to a president stands next in line and may step up to lead.

clue.text: Tree-lined street, not a place to stage a concert

indicators.note: not a means leave the letter A out

parts.note: an avenue is a broad street, often lined with trees

explanation.surface: A leafy road is no spot for an open-air gig.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall or arena where events are held is a site.

clue.text: Old man's half-hearted spiel

indicators.note: half-hearted removes half of the double letter at the word's heart

parts.note: spiel is patter, a glib sales talk

explanation.surface: Dad gives a feeble sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one of the two middle Ts of PATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pater is Latin for father, old-fashioned British public-school slang for one's dad.

clue.text: Woman brought up in East Timor, for example

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means written upwards, so the letters reverse

parts.note: Timor is an island, an isle

explanation.surface: A woman raised in the eastern part of an Asian island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns E + ISLE into ELSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name stands for any woman.

clue.text: Supporter admitted to international is a child

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside the word

parts.note: a fan is a supporter

explanation.surface: A fan allowed into a big match turns out to be a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby or very young person is a little one.

clue.text: Not being in favour of sitting after work

indicators.note: after says the sitting piece follows the work piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
sitting for a portrait is posing

explanation.surface: An artist's model refuses to sit once a job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Being against something is resisting it.

clue.text: I certainly get taken about, having lots of time to relax?

definitions.text: having lots of time to relax?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the others

parts.note: to be taken somewhere is to be led
sure means certainly

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of being chauffeured around with ample spare time.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with plenty of free time and no need to work is idle and at ease.

clue.text: Town with old English name, abbreviated

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: abbreviated means the word is shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a term is a name for something

explanation.surface: A place keeps its ancient English title in shortened form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' cuts TERM to TER. Exeter is the county town of Devon in south-west England (strictly a city).
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is a Devon cathedral settlement, a town in the loose sense.
